<!-- thm-1: body_md -->
\label{main thm}
   Let $q$ be a fixed odd prime power and $\kappa \geq 0$ be any fixed real number.  Set 
   \[
   \sigma= \frac12+\frac{\kappa}{\ln g}.
   \]
   For any $\epsilon\in (0,1/2)$,  we obtain, as $g \to \infty$, 
    \[
    \max_{P \in \mathcal{P}_{2g+1}} |L(\sigma, \chi_P)| 
    \gg \exp \left( \left(  e^{-\kappa} \,\ln q \,  \sqrt{\frac{\sqrt{q}+1}{\sqrt{q}-1} (1/2-\epsilon)}  + o(1) \right) 
\sqrt{\frac{g \ln_2 g}{\ln g}} \right).
    \]
<!-- end thm-1 -->
<!-- rem-1: body_md -->
For the rational function field $F=\mathbb F_q[t]$, our leading
	constant is larger than the corresponding constant in
	\cite[Theorem~1.3]{dong2026}, provided that $\varepsilon>0$ is chosen
	sufficiently small. We note, however, that the theorem of Dong and Liu
	applies to arbitrary fixed global function fields and also shows that
	many principal primes $P$ give rise to quadratic characters $\chi_P$
	with large $L$-values.
<!-- end rem-1 -->
<!-- rem-2: body_md -->
For $P\in\mathcal{P}_{2g+2}$, it seems difficult to obtain results of
	the same strength as Theorem~\ref{main thm}  by the present method.
	Indeed, in the even-degree case we have $\lambda=1$, and the
	approximate functional equation contains additional $\lambda$-terms (see \cite[Lemma 7]{darbar2024}).
	These extra terms do not preserve the positivity used in our
	resonator argument. Therefore, our present approach does not directly
	give the same lower bounds for the family
	$\{L(\sigma,\chi_P):P\in\mathcal{P}_{2g+2}\}$.
<!-- end rem-2 -->
<!-- thm-2: body_md -->
\label{thm inside critical strip}
	Let $q$ be a fixed odd prime power and $\beta_q(\sigma,b), \alpha_q(b)$ be as defined in \eqref{assumtion}. Then, for every sufficiently large  $\mathbf{N}$, there exists a polynomial  $P \in \mathcal{P}_\mathbf{N}$ such that
	\begin{equation*}\label{lower bound inside strip}
		\ln L(\sigma,\chi_P) \geq (\beta_q(\sigma,b)+o(1))\frac{ ( \log |P|)^{1-\sigma}}{(\log \log |P|)^{\sigma}}.
	\end{equation*}
	 Furthermore, for every  $	0<\xi<\frac{1}{\alpha_q(b)},$
	define
	$
		\tau_{\xi,\mathbf N}
		:=
		\beta_q(\sigma,b)
		\left(1-\xi\alpha_q(b)\right)^{1-\sigma}
		{\mathbf N^{1-\sigma}}
		{(\log\mathbf N)^{ -\sigma}},
	$ such that 
	\begin{equation*}
		\Phi_{\mathbf N}(\sigma,\xi)
		:=
		\frac{1}{	\# \mathcal P_{\mathbf N} }
		\#\left\{
		P\in\mathcal P_{\mathbf N}:
		\ln L(\sigma,\chi_P)
		\geq \tau_{\xi,\mathbf N}
		\right\}.
	\end{equation*}
		Then, for sufficiently large $\mathbf N$,
	\begin{equation*}
		\Phi_{\mathbf N}(\sigma,\xi)
		\geq
		|P|^{-\frac{1}{2}
			(1-\xi\alpha_q(b))+o(1)}.
	\end{equation*}
<!-- end thm-2 -->
<!-- rem-3: body_md -->
Letting $ b \to 1$ in the above theorem, we obtain
	\[
	\beta_q(\sigma,b)=\mathcal{Z}(2-\sigma) \left( \frac{\ln q}{2 \mathcal{Z}(2)q \ln 2} \right) ^{1-\sigma}.
	\]
	This improves the constant 
	$
	\beta'_q(\sigma) = {\mathcal{Z}(2-\sigma)}{(10 q \mathcal{Z}(2))^{\sigma-1}},
	$
	obtained by Lumley \cite{lumley2021}. Thus, our result gives the same order of magnitude as Lumley's
	$\Omega$-result \eqref{lumley rel}, with a strictly larger leading constant.
<!-- end rem-3 -->
<!-- lem-1: body_md -->
\label{ApproximateFE}
Suppose that $P\in\mathcal{P}_{2g+1}$ and let $\chi_P$ denote the corresponding quadratic Dirichlet character. Then
\[
L\left(s,\chi_P\right)
=
\sum_{A\in\mathcal{M}_{\leq g}}
\frac{\chi_P(A)}{|A|^s}
+ q^{g(1-2s)}
\sum_{A\in\mathcal{M}_{\leq g-1}}
\frac{\chi_P(A)}{|A|^{1-s}}.
\]
<!-- end lem-1 -->
<!-- proof-1: body_md -->
See	\cite[Eq.~(3.23)]{andra2012}.
<!-- end proof-1 -->
<!-- lem-2: body_md -->
\label{weil}
For any non-square polynomial $A\in\mathcal{M}$ and any positive integer $n$,
\[
\left|
\sum_{P\in\mathcal{P}_n}\chi_P(A)
\right|
\ll
\frac{q^{n/2}}{n}\mathbf{d}(A).
\]
<!-- end lem-2 -->
<!-- proof-2: body_md -->
See \cite[Eq.~(2.5)]{rudnick2010}.
<!-- end proof-2 -->
<!-- lem-3: body_md -->
\label{prime pol thm}
	Assume that $n$ is a large positive integer. Then
\[
\pi_q(n)= \frac{q^n}{n} + O\left(\frac{q^{n/2}}{n}\right), \quad\text{and} \quad
\pi_q(n) \leq \frac{q^n}{n}.
\]
<!-- end lem-3 -->
<!-- proof-3: body_md -->
See \cite[Theorem~2.2]{rosen2002}.
<!-- end proof-3 -->
<!-- lem-4: body_md -->
\label{char sum}
Let $A \in \mathcal{M}$. Then
\[
\sum_{P \in \mathcal{P}_n} \chi_P(A^2) = \frac{q^n}{n} + O\left(\frac{q^{n/2}}{n}\right) + O(\log \log \mathbf{d}(A)).
\]
<!-- end lem-4 -->
<!-- proof-4: body_md -->
See \cite[Lemma~5]{darbar2024}.
<!-- end proof-4 -->
<!-- lem-5: body_md -->
\label{produc of poly}
Assume that $0\le s<1$. Then, for a large positive integer $n$,
\[
\sum_{P \in \mathcal{P}_{\leq n}} \frac{1}{|P|^s}
= \mathcal{Z}(2-s)\frac{q^{n(1-s)}}{n}\left(1 + O\left(\frac{\ln n}{n}\right)\right).
\]
For the special case $s=0$, one obtains
\[
\Pi_q(n) = \mathcal{Z}(2)\frac{q^n}{n}\left(1 + O\left(\frac{\ln n}{n}\right)\right).
\]
<!-- end lem-5 -->
<!-- proof-5: body_md -->
See	\cite[Lemma~3.2]{dokic2020}.
<!-- end proof-5 -->
<!-- prop-1: body_md -->
\label{prop}
	Let $q$ be a fixed odd prime power and let
	\[
	\sigma=\frac12+\frac{\kappa}{\ln_2 \mathcal{N}},
	\qquad \kappa\geq 0.
	\]
	Then, uniformly for $\kappa$ in any fixed compact subset of
	$[0,\infty)$, for all sufficiently large $\mathcal{N}$, there exists
	a set $\mathfrak{R}$ of monic squarefree polynomials with
	$|\mathfrak{R}|=\mathcal{N}$ such that
	\[
	S_{\sigma}(\mathfrak{R})
	\geq
	\mathcal{N}
	\exp\left\{
	\left(
	e^{-\kappa}
	\sqrt{\frac{\sqrt{q}+1}{\sqrt{q}-1}\ln q}
	+o(1)
	\right)
	\sqrt{
		\frac{\ln \mathcal{N}\ln_3 \mathcal{N}}
		{\ln_2 \mathcal{N}}
	}
	\right\}.
	\]
<!-- end prop-1 -->
<!-- lem-6: body_md -->
\label{card R}
Under the condition \eqref{condition}, we have
$ |\mathfrak{R}|\leq \mathcal{N}$.
<!-- end lem-6 -->
